correctness.rationale: I solved the degree-one to degree-four interpolation moment equations directly in first differences, and formed the product of the three resulting companions. Its cubic z³+az²+bz+c gives a=2U/D,b=V/D,c=−W/D, with D>0. The replay verifies positivity of the three other cubic Schur expressions by positive coefficients and 1−a+b−c=−8(R+3)P/D. Descartes' rule and the signs at 59 and 60 certify the unique positive zero; a negative-axis intermediate-value argument gives a root below −1 for every larger R. At the boundary write q=(z+1)(z²+Bz+C), with B=a−1 and C=c. The quadratic has |C|<1, 1+B+C=q(1)/2>0, and 1−B+C=(1−b+ac−c²)/(1−C)>0, so −1 is simple. The full-value monodromy also has the separate constant multiplier 1; since 1 is absent from the difference spectrum throughout the power-bounded interval, no Jordan coupling at 1 can cause growth. Independent row power limits and direct characteristic coefficients recover the limiting singular polynomial; the nonzero factor has |b_lim|<1, 1+a_lim+b_lim>0 and 1−a_lim+b_lim=8(2−s)/(7(s+2)). At s=2 its roots are −1 and −1/14. Continuity of the cubic roots gives the asserted large-R finite-grid conclusions for fixed s≠2, not a finite-R classification at s=2.
residual_risks: These are fixed-pattern homogeneous Floquet results. They are not an arbitrary-grid stability bound, a convergence theorem on nonzero ODEs, or a result about finite R at the singular frontier s=2.

evidence: Söderlind–Fekete–Faragó require meshes from smooth deformations, with adjacent ratios 1+O(N⁻¹). Calvo–Grande–Grigorieff was identified as a broader variable order/stepsize BDF zero-stability work, but the primary full text was not obtained.
broader_coverage.reasoning: A fixed nonuniform repeating pattern fails the smooth-grid ratio hypothesis for large N even after common scaling. Sufficient general mesh-ratio bounds alone would not imply a necessary-and-sufficient Floquet threshold or its limiting spectrum; the exact specialist comparison with Calvo et al. remains open.

value.rationale: A high-contrast periodic grid can expose an exact instability missed by looking only at generic sufficient smoothness/ratio guarantees. The explicit finite boundary distinguishes parasitic damping, neutral power-boundedness and exponential growth for the entire one-parameter slice. The larger singular family motivates the choice of 3 as the first integer above the limiting frontier 2, and gives an actual stability prediction for sufficiently large contrasts on either side of that frontier.
residual_risks: No claims about general-grid convergence or practical time-stepping control follow without further analysis.
